response: The use of audit to identify maternal mortality in different settings is not just a difference between the rich and the poor. While socioeconomic factors do play a role in maternal mortality, it is a complex issue that requires a multifaceted approach. Acknowledging the magnitude of maternal mortality and harnessing a strong political will to tackle the issues are important factors. Audit, both national and local, is essential in identifying problems and promoting solutions to reduce maternal mortality. There is no single, general solution to reduce maternal mortality, and a comprehensive approach that takes into account various factors, including healthcare access, education, and economic empowerment, is necessary to address this issue effectively.
